patch_description: The current algorithm computes one shortest path per destination and assigns every partition to that same path. This overloads a single route (its per-edge throughput cap gets violated, driving costs up) and ignores cheaper parallel alternatives across networks. Improvement: for each destination, consider the K shortest simple paths (by cost), and distribute partitions across them in a load-balanced round-robin fashion. This spreads flow over multiple egress links, keeps per-edge load under throughput constraints, and exploits low-cost parallel routes in multi-network topologies. We also remove a bug: incoming edges to src are removed from a graph copy, but edge metadata `G[s][t]` is still fetched from the original G — keep that, but now compute candidate paths with an effective-cost weight that penalizes congested edges so load balancing emerges naturally.
